Temporal and contemporaneous networks of a continuous time model

Source: R/ctGraph.R
ctNetwork.Rd

Computes the directed temporal network and the undirected contemporaneous network used in network psychometrics, from a ctsem model specification or from a fit on either backend.

In a continuous time model both networks depend on the time interval, and their shape as well as their scale changes with dt.

Usage

ctNetwork(
  x,
  dt = 1,
  state = NULL,
  standardise = TRUE,
  impulseType = "unit",
  threshold = 0,
  networks = c("temporal", "contemporaneous"),
  plot = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE,
  ...,
  observational
)

Arguments

x

A ctStanModel from ctModel, or a fit from ctFit on either backend.

dt

Time interval for the temporal and contemporaneous networks, a whole number of steps for a discrete time model. A single value. To compare intervals, call ctNetworkPlot with a vector.

state

Where state dependent cells are evaluated, when x is a fit: 'T0MEANS' (the default, as in ctSummaryMatrices), 'mean' for the mean smoothed latent state, 'asymptotic' for the system's fixed point, or a numeric state vector. Values other than the default need backend='julia' and are an error for a stan fit. No effect for a linear model or an unfitted specification.

standardise

If TRUE (the default), temporal edges are in standard deviation units of the processes, using asymDIFFUSIONcov, so edges between processes on different scales are comparable. Set to FALSE, with a message, when the system has no stationary variance.

impulseType

What a one unit change in a process brings with it; see ctDiscretePars. 'unit' (the default) changes that process alone, giving the partial regression.

threshold

Edges with abs(weight) at or below this are dropped from $edges and from any plot. The matrices are not thresholded.

networks

Which networks appear in $edges and in the plot. Any of 'temporal', 'contemporaneous', 'asymptotic', 'measurement'. All four matrices are always computed.

plot

If TRUE, returns the ctNetworkPlot of the result instead of the result.

quiet

Suppress the messages about how the numbers were computed.

...

Passed to ctSummaryMatrices when x is a fit, and to ctNetworkPlot when plot=TRUE.

observational

Deprecated. Use impulseType.

Value

A list of class ctNetwork:

temporal, contemporaneous, asymptotic, measurement

Weight matrices with the model's names, in the form qgraph::qgraph() takes. asymptotic may be NULL.

edges

Data frame with columns network, from, to, weight, directed and self, thresholded and restricted to networks.

nodes

Data frame of name and type ('latent' or 'manifest').

DRIFT, DIFFUSIONcov, asymDIFFUSIONcov, innovation

The matrices the networks were computed from. On a julia fit DRIFT is the drift's Jacobian at the evaluation point, which equals DRIFT when no cell depends on the state.

With attributes dt, standardise, impulseType, threshold, networks, continuoustime, source, stateLabel (the evaluation point, for a fit) and stateDependent (the state dependent cells, or NULL).

Details

Three networks over the latent processes, plus the measurement model:

temporal

expm(DRIFT * dt), the discrete time autoregressive and cross-lagged matrix at interval dt. Directed, with the autoregressions as self-loops on the diagonal. Cell [i,j] is the effect of process j now on process i one interval later, so an edge runs from the column to the row. This is ctDiscretePars at a single interval, with the same impulseType and standardise arguments.

contemporaneous

Partial correlations of the innovation covariance accumulated over dt, Q(dt) = int_0^dt expm(DRIFT s) DIFFUSIONcov t(expm(DRIFT s)) ds. This is the continuous time counterpart of the graphicalVAR contemporaneous network. As dt shrinks it tends to the partial correlations of DIFFUSIONcov, and as dt grows to those of the asymptotic covariance.

asymptotic

Partial correlations of asymDIFFUSIONcov, the long run within-subject covariance. This is the network a cross-sectional study of a stationary system would find. NULL if the system is not stationary.

measurement

LAMBDA, as a bipartite manifest by latent graph, directed from latent to manifest.

From a fit, the matrices are the posterior medians that ctSummaryMatrices reports. From an unfitted specification, a fixed cell takes its value, and a free cell takes the value its transform gives at a raw parameter of zero. The number of DRIFT, DIFFUSION and LAMBDA cells set this way is reported.

State dependent and nonlinear models

When a DRIFT, DIFFUSION or LAMBDA cell is an expression of a latent process, the network differs across the state space. The networks reported for a fit are those of the system linearised at one point, and elsewhere the edge weights differ, as can which edges are present. The temporal and contemporaneous networks then use the drift's Jacobian at that point (JAx), and the measurement network uses the measurement Jacobian (Jy). These differ from DRIFT and LAMBDA where a cell is nonlinear in the state: a cell a + b*Y in the column of process Y has slope a + 2*b*Y. A stan fit has no Jacobians, so its edges are the cells' values at T0MEANS, with a message saying so.

When such cells are present, ctNetwork gives a message naming the evaluation point, and records the cells in attr(x, 'stateDependent'). ctNetworkPlot puts the point in the plot's subtitle. Use state to change the point, and ctPhasePortrait or ctStateDependencePlot to see how the system varies over the state space. For a linear model there is no message.

From an unfitted specification such cells are reported and left out.

See also

ctNetworkPlot to draw it, ctDiscretePars for the temporal network over a range of intervals, ctPhasePortrait and ctStateDependencePlot for how a state dependent system varies away from the evaluation point.

Examples

# Two processes, b driven by a, drawn at one interval.
m <- ctModel(type='ct', n.latent=2, n.manifest=2,
  manifestNames=c('y1','y2'), latentNames=c('a','b'),
  LAMBDA=diag(2),
  DRIFT=matrix(c(-1, 0, .5, -2), 2, 2, byrow=TRUE),
  DIFFUSION=matrix(c(1, 0, .3, 1), 2, 2, byrow=TRUE))

net <- ctNetwork(m, dt=1, standardise=FALSE)
round(net$temporal, 4)          # exp(-1) and exp(-2) on the diagonal
round(net$contemporaneous, 4)
net$edges
